note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in CA.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Route 1, San Mateo County
byways.where: SR 1 from the Santa Cruz County line north to the south city limit of Half Moon Bay (PM 0.0 to 26.2), San Mateo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 1 from the Santa Cruz county line to the south city limit of Half Moon Bay as officially designated on June 25, 1976 (designation no. 39).
Entering San Mateo County, SR 1 follows the coast past the marine mammal colonies at Año Nuevo State Park and the historic Pigeon Point Lighthouse before reaching Half Moon Bay.

byways.review: The catalog entry pacific-coast-highway-california-s-route-1-12744 covers all of Route 1 and is not a state designation, so it is not matched here.

byways.name: Route 1, Big Sur Coast (Monterey County)
byways.where: SR 1 from the San Luis Obispo County line north through Big Sur to the Carmel River, and on to Route 68 in Monterey (PM 0.0 to R78.1), Monterey County

facts.fact: Route 1 from the San Luis Obispo county line to the Carmel River carries Caltrans designation no. 1, dated June 7, 1965; the Carmel River to Route 68 stretch followed on May 21, 1970.
The Big Sur coast road was declared the first State Scenic Highway in 1965, and in 1966 Lady Bird Johnson led the designation ceremony at Bixby Bridge.
For about 72 miles from San Carpóforo Creek to Malpaso Creek the road hugs the Big Sur cliffs, crossing Bixby Bridge, a concrete arch with a 320-foot span over the Bixby Creek gorge.

byways.review: Two Caltrans designations merged here: SLO county line to Carmel River (no. 1, 1965) and Carmel River to Route 68 (no. 14, 1970). The url is the Big Sur Chamber of Commerce, the nearest thing to a byway organization; no agency page found.

byways.name: Route 1, San Luis Obispo North Coast
byways.where: SR 1 from the San Luis Obispo city limit north to the Monterey County line (PM 17.7 to 74.3), San Luis Obispo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 1 from the San Luis Obispo city limit to the Monterey county line as officially designated on August 13, 1999.
North of San Luis Obispo the highway runs through Cambria and San Simeon, past the elephant seal colony at Piedras Blancas Light Station, and gives access to Hearst Castle.

byways.name: Route 1, Santa Barbara County (Las Cruces to Lompoc)
byways.where: SR 1 (Cabrillo Highway) from US 101 near Las Cruces northwest to near Lompoc (PM R0.0 to 18.5), Santa Barbara County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 1 from Route 101 near Las Cruces to near Lompoc as officially designated on December 14, 1971.
At Las Cruces SR 1, named the Cabrillo Highway, splits from US 101 and heads northwest to Lompoc.
An interchange of US 101 and SR 1 was built at Las Cruces in 1967, destroying the town.

byways.name: Route 2, Angeles Crest Highway
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Forest Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SR 2 from 2.7 miles north of Route 210 at La Cañada Flintridge to the San Bernardino County line (PM 27.2 to 82.3), Los Angeles County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 2 from 2.7 miles north of Route 210 to the San Bernardino county line as officially designated on March 12, 1971.
The highway climbs to a high point of 7,903 feet at Dawson Saddle.
The stretch between Islip Saddle and Vincent Gap is generally closed from mid-December to mid-May for snow and rockfall.

byways.name: Route 4, Ebbetts Pass
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SR 4 from east of Arnold over Ebbetts Pass to Route 89 near Markleeville (Calaveras PM 41.6 to R65.9; Alpine PM R0.0 to 31.7), Calaveras and Alpine counties

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 4 east of Arnold to the Alpine county line (November 9, 1971) and from the Calaveras county line to Route 89 (September 14, 1970) as officially designated.
Beyond the Mount Reba turnoff to Bear Valley the road becomes steep and single-track with no center line, and it crosses 8,730-foot Ebbetts Pass.
Ebbetts Pass is not plowed and usually closes from November until as late as May.

byways.name: Routes 5 and 580, West Side Freeway
byways.where: I-5 from Route 152 north through Merced and Stanislaus counties to I-580, and I-580 from I-5 to Route 205 (San Joaquin and Alameda counties)

facts.fact: Caltrans lists I-5 from Route 152 through Stanislaus County (October 25, 1968) and I-580 from I-5 to Route 205 (1970 and 1974) as officially designated.
Between its Utica Avenue exit and I-580, I-5 parallels the eastern foothills of the Diablo Range and crosses the California Aqueduct between SR 152 and SR 33 and again near Crows Landing.
I-580 splits from I-5 south of Tracy and meets I-205 near Altamont Raceway Park.

byways.review: Five Caltrans segments merged (I-5 in Merced, Stanislaus and San Joaquin counties; I-580 in San Joaquin and Alameda counties).

byways.name: Route 9, Saratoga-Los Gatos Road
byways.where: SR 9 from the Santa Cruz County line at Saratoga Gap to the Los Gatos town limit (PM 0.0 to 10.8), Santa Clara County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 9 from Blaney Plaza in Saratoga to the Los Gatos city limit (May 2, 1968) and from Saratoga Gap to Blaney Plaza (October 18, 1979) as officially designated.
The seven-mile section from Saratoga Village to Saratoga Gap is known for the number of cyclists climbing it on weekend mornings.
A vista point at the SR 35 junction, around 2,608 feet, is the route's highest point.

byways.name: Route 12, Valley of the Moon (Sonoma County)
byways.where: SR 12 from Danielli Avenue east of Santa Rosa to London Way near Agua Caliente (PM 22.3 to 33.9), Sonoma County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 12 from Danielli Avenue east of Santa Rosa to London Way near Agua Caliente as officially designated on December 17, 1974.
Past Santa Rosa the highway turns south into the Sonoma Valley, passing Jack London State Historic Park at Glen Ellen; the Sonoma County portion is known as the Valley of the Moon Scenic Route.

byways.review: The catalog line (21 mi) runs a little beyond the designated 11.6 miles.

byways.name: Route 20, Nevada County
byways.where: SR 20 from Skillman Flat Campground to 0.5 mile east of Lowell Hill Road (PM 33.0 to 39.5), Nevada County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 20 from Skillman Flat Campground to half a mile east of Lowell Hill Road as officially designated on March 12, 1971.

East of Nevada City the road follows Harmony Ridge and Washington Ridge, and the Pioneer Trail, a National Recreation Trail including parts of a branch of the California Trail first used in 1850, parallels it toward Bear Valley.

byways.name: Route 24, Contra Costa County
byways.where: SR 24 from the east portal of the Caldecott Tunnel to I-680 in Walnut Creek (PM R0.3 to 9.1), Contra Costa County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 24 from the east portal of the Caldecott Tunnel to I-680 at Walnut Creek as officially designated on October 22, 1982.
In Contra Costa County the freeway passes through wooded hillsides and suburbs, with BART in the median except near the Caldecott Tunnel and the I-680 approach.
The Caldecott Tunnel opened in 1937 with two bores; it has had four since 2013.

byways.review: The catalog names this road "Route 24--Alameda County", but the designated segment is entirely in Contra Costa County (catalog line is in the right place).

byways.name: Route 27, Topanga Canyon Boulevard
byways.where: SR 27 from 1.0 to 3.5 miles north of Route 1 in Topanga Canyon, Los Angeles County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists the Topanga Canyon State Scenic Highway on Route 27 (PM 1.0 to 3.5) as officially designated on March 22, 2017.
From SR 1 at Topanga State Beach, Topanga Canyon Boulevard runs north through Topanga State Park and winds through the Santa Monica Mountains.

byways.name: Route 33, Maricopa Highway (Ventura County)
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Forest Scenic Byway, Jacinto Reyes)
byways.where: SR 33 from 6.4 miles north of Route 150 to the Santa Barbara County line (PM 17.6 to 57.5), Ventura County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists four Route 33 segments from 6.4 miles north of Route 150 to the Santa Barbara county line, designated February 18, 1972 and July 11, 1988.
North of Ojai the Maricopa Highway follows Matilija Canyon into Los Padres National Forest and crosses the Transverse Ranges at Pine Mountain Summit.
The Reyes family largely mapped the current route to reach the coast from their ranch on the Cuyama side of the mountains.

byways.name: Route 35, Skyline Boulevard
byways.where: SR 35 from the Santa Cruz County line to Route 92 (PM 0.0 to 23.0), San Mateo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 35 from the Santa Cruz county line to Route 92 as officially designated in 1968 (January 22 and September 13).
Skyline Boulevard follows the ridge of the Santa Cruz Mountains and passes through the small community of Sky Londa, where it meets SR 84.
Because of its views and winding road, Skyline Boulevard sees heavy recreational motorcycling and cycling.

byways.name: Route 38, San Bernardino Mountains
byways.where: SR 38 from 0.1 mile east of South Fork Campground to 2.9 miles south of Route 18 at State Lane (PM 31.0 to 46.6), San Bernardino County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 38 from just east of South Fork Campground to 2.9 miles south of Route 18 as officially designated on March 19, 1968 (designation no. 3).
SR 38 reaches Onyx Summit at 8,443 feet, where it is one of the highest roads in southern California.
The Rim of the World Scenic Byway includes portions of Highways 138, 18 and 38, and the stretch between Mill Creek and Onyx Summit looks over the Sand to Snow National Monument.

byways.review: This segment is part of the USFS Rim of the World Scenic Byway (catalog rim-of-the-world-scenic-byway-2595), but the catalog line is the whole 100-mile forest byway, so it is listed under the USFS program instead.

byways.name: Route 49, Sierra County
byways.where: SR 49 from the Yuba County line to Yuba Summit (PM 0.0 to 41.2), Sierra County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 49 from the Yuba county line to Yuba Summit as officially designated on July 14, 1971.
In Sierra County SR 49 passes through Goodyears Bar, Downieville and Sierra City through forested terrain; this stretch also forms part of the Yuba-Donner Scenic Byway.
SR 49 runs through the mining communities of the 1849 gold rush and is known as the Golden Chain Highway.

byways.review: Also part of the USFS Yuba-Donner Scenic Byway, which is not in the catalog.

byways.name: Route 50, El Dorado County
byways.where: US 50 from the Government Center interchange in Placerville over Echo Summit to the South Lake Tahoe city limit (PM 16.8 to 74.4), El Dorado County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists US 50 from Placerville to Echo Summit (April 2, 1985) and from Echo Summit to the South Lake Tahoe city limit (April 1, 1986) as officially designated.
East of Pollock Pines the highway enters the canyon of the South Fork American River, passes Kyburz, and climbs hairpin turns east of Strawberry to Echo Summit.
The corridor was used by many forty-niners and by the Pony Express.

byways.name: Route 52, Mission Trails
byways.where: SR 52 freeway from near Santo Road to near Mast Boulevard (PM 9.5 to 13.0), San Diego

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 52 from near Santo Road to near Mast Boulevard as officially designated on February 2, 2016.

Between Santo Road and Mast Boulevard the freeway crosses Mission Trails Regional Park, climbing to Mission Trails Pass north of 1,230-foot Fortuna Mountain, with a two-way bicycle path on its north side.

byways.name: Route 62, Twentynine Palms Highway
byways.where: SR 62 from I-10 to the San Bernardino County line (PM 0.0 to 9.2), Riverside County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 62 from I-10 to the San Bernardino county line as officially designated on September 14, 1972.
SR 62 begins at I-10 at the eastern end of San Gorgonio Pass northwest of Palm Springs; the part from Whitewater to Morongo Valley joined the state system in 1935.

byways.name: Route 68, Monterey-Salinas Highway
byways.where: SR 68 from Route 1 in Monterey to the Salinas River (PM R4.0 to R17.8), Monterey County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 68 from Route 1 in Monterey to the Salinas River as officially designated on June 19, 1968.
The 14 miles from Route 1 to the Salinas River are a scenic route for their views of chaparral and springtime lupine; the road passes Laguna Seca raceway, Laureles Grade and Corral de Tierra.

byways.name: Routes 74 and 243, Palms to Pines
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Forest Scenic Byway, Palms to Pines)
byways.where: SR 74 from the San Bernardino National Forest boundary to Route 111 at Palm Desert (PM 48.3 to R92.3) and SR 243 from Route 74 to the Banning city limit (PM 0.0 to 28.2), Riverside County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 74 from the national forest boundary to Route 111 (October 18, 1971) and Route 243 from Route 74 to Banning (March 21, 1972) as officially designated.
SR 74 climbs from Palm Desert along Deep Canyon through Pinyon Pines, crosses the Santa Rosa Indian Reservation, and runs through Garner Valley to Mountain Center.
SR 243, the Banning-Idyllwild Panoramic Highway, runs from Mountain Center through Idyllwild and switchbacks down to Banning.

byways.review: Two Caltrans designations (Route 74, no. 25; Route 243, no. 33) merged to match the single catalog road. The GIS feature for Route 74 has identical begin and end coordinates, but its line has a real length.

byways.name: Route 75, Silver Strand and Coronado Bridge
byways.where: SR 75 from the Imperial Beach city limit along the Silver Strand to Avenida del Sol in Coronado, and the San Diego-Coronado Bridge, San Diego County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists the San Diego-Coronado Bridge (December 17, 1969) and Route 75 from Imperial Beach to Avenida del Sol (March 4, 1974) as officially designated.
The Silver Strand is a thin strip of land between the Pacific Ocean and San Diego Bay; the highway runs along it through Silver Strand State Beach.
The 2.1-mile bridge, opened in 1969, curves 80 degrees so it can give Navy ships 200 feet of clearance at a reasonable grade.

byways.name: Route 78, Anza-Borrego Desert State Park
byways.where: SR 78 from the west to the east boundary of Anza-Borrego Desert State Park (PM 71.9 to 90.1), San Diego County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 78 across Anza-Borrego Desert State Park as officially designated on December 14, 1971.
Just after Scissors Crossing, SR 78 enters Anza-Borrego Desert State Park and runs through Ocotillo Wells before leaving the park.
The Old Banner Toll Road linked Julian and Banner in 1871, after a gold rush began in 1870.

byways.name: Route 84, Niles Canyon Road
byways.where: SR 84 from Route 238 in Fremont to I-680 near Sunol (PM 10.8 to 18.0), Alameda County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 84 from Route 238 to I-680 near Sunol as officially designated on July 7, 2007.
Niles Canyon Road follows the canyon cut by Alameda Creek between the Niles district of Fremont and Sunol; the old Southern Pacific line on the north side is now the Niles Canyon Railway.
The Essanay film company had a studio and back lot at the canyon's western mouth from 1912 to 1916.

byways.name: Route 88, Carson Pass Highway
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Forest Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SR 88 from the Dew Drop ranger station over Carson Pass to the Nevada state line (Amador PM R38.3 to 71.6; Alpine PM 0.0 to 25.3), Amador and Alpine counties

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 88 from the Amador county line to the Nevada state line (September 14, 1970) and from Dew Drop Ranger Station to the Alpine county line (July 30, 1986) as officially designated.
The road passes Kirkwood and Caples Lake on the climb to Carson Pass, then descends past a view of Red Lake into Hope Valley and down Woodfords Canyon.
The path over Carson Pass was used earlier by the California Trail and the Mormon Emigrant Trail.

byways.name: Route 89, Monitor Pass, Luther Pass and Lake Tahoe
byways.where: SR 89 from 3.2 miles west of US 395 over Monitor Pass, through Alpine County and over Luther Pass, and along Lake Tahoe to the Placer County line (Mono, Alpine and El Dorado counties)

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 89 from 3.2 miles west of Route 395 to the Placer county line in three segments, designated 1970, 1971 and 1986.
The road climbs to 8,314-foot Monitor Pass, drops to the Carson River at Markleeville and Woodfords, and crosses 7,740-foot Luther Pass.
Along the western shore of Lake Tahoe it passes Camp Richardson and Emerald Bay.

byways.name: Route 91, Riverside Freeway (Orange County)
byways.where: SR 91 from Route 55 to the east Anaheim city limit (PM R9.2 to R14.4), Orange County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 91 from Route 55 to the east Anaheim city limit as officially designated on November 15, 1971.
The designated part lies in the western Santa Ana Canyon; the rest of the canyon to I-15 is only eligible.

byways.review: The catalog line is 37.6 miles and runs into Riverside County; the designated segment is only about 4 to 5 miles. Consider replacing with the Caltrans line.

byways.name: Route 101, Del Norte Coast Redwoods
byways.where: US 101 through Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park toward Crescent City (PM 11.0 to 23.1), Del Norte County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 101 from the south to the north boundary of Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park as officially designated on February 18, 1970.
US 101 is designated through Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park and traverses Last Chance Grade as it approaches Crescent City; Caltrans has proposed a tunnel to replace the grade.

byways.name: Route 101, Gaviota Coast
byways.where: US 101 from near Goleta west along the Gaviota Coast and north through Gaviota Pass to Route 1 at Las Cruces (PM 27.5 to R48.9), Santa Barbara County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists the Gaviota Coast State Scenic Highway on Route 101, from near Goleta to Route 1 at Las Cruces, as officially designated on December 13, 2016.

West of Goleta, US 101 follows a 19-mile stretch of the Gaviota Coast, often directly overlooking the shore, then turns north through Gaviota Pass, where only the northbound lanes use the Gaviota Tunnel.
El Capitán State Beach, Refugio State Beach and Gaviota State Park line the highway along this coast.

byways.name: Route 116, Sonoma County
byways.where: SR 116 from Route 1 near Jenner to the south city limit of Sebastopol (PM 0.0 to 27.9), Sonoma County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 116 from Route 1 to the south city limit of Sebastopol as officially designated on September 20, 1988.

SR 116 follows the north bank of the Russian River from SR 1 through Duncans Mills, Monte Rio and Guerneville, then runs through Pocket Canyon to Forestville and becomes the Gravenstein Highway to Sebastopol.

byways.name: Route 125, La Mesa
byways.where: SR 125 from Route 94 near Spring Valley to I-8 near La Mesa (PM 13.5 to R15.4), San Diego County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 125 from Route 94 to I-8 as officially designated on March 1, 1971.
The City of La Mesa began discussing adding SR 125 from SR 94 to I-8 to the scenic highway system in 1968.

byways.name: Route 140, Mariposa County
byways.where: SR 140 from north of the Mariposa town planning area to west of El Portal (PM 22.8 to 49.9), Mariposa County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 140 from north of Mariposa to west of El Portal as officially designated on September 30, 1991.
Ponderosa pines line the highway through Midpines before it drops down a steep grade to Briceburg and follows the Merced River toward El Portal.
The "All-Year Highway", now SR 140, opened on July 31, 1926 on the south bank of the Merced, opposite the Yosemite Valley Railroad, as the first all-season road to Yosemite.

byways.review: The catalog line (44 mi) is longer than the designated 27 miles.

byways.name: Route 151, Shasta Dam Boulevard
byways.where: SR 151 from Shasta Dam to near Lake Boulevard (PM 0.0 to 3.3), Shasta County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 151 from Shasta Dam to near Lake Boulevard as officially designated on September 9, 1981.
State maintenance begins at the visitor center south of Shasta Dam, and the road heads south through heavily vegetated country.
Shasta Dam is 602 feet high and impounds Shasta Lake, the largest reservoir in California.

byways.name: Route 152, Pacheco Pass Road (Merced County)
byways.where: SR 152 from the Santa Clara County line to I-5 (PM R0.0 to 13.8), Merced County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 152 from the Santa Clara county line to I-5 as officially designated on June 19, 1970.
East of Pacheco Pass the highway descends along the north and east shore of San Luis Reservoir, between San Luis Dam and the O'Neill Forebay.
Pacheco Pass, at 1,368 feet, had a station on the Butterfield Overland Mail stage route from 1858 to 1861.

byways.name: Route 154, San Marcos Pass Road
byways.where: SR 154 from US 101 near Los Olivos over San Marcos Pass to US 101 in Santa Barbara (PM R0.0 to 32.3), Santa Barbara County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 154 from Route 101 near Los Olivos via San Marcos Pass to Route 101 in Santa Barbara as officially designated on November 22, 1968.

SR 154, also called the Chumash Highway, passes Lake Cachuma, runs through Los Padres National Forest and crosses the Cold Spring Canyon Arch Bridge, below which Cold Spring Tavern sits on Stagecoach Road.

byways.name: Route 156, Castroville to Prunedale
byways.where: SR 156 from Route 183 one mile east of Castroville to US 101 near Prunedale (PM R1.0 to T5.2), Monterey County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 156 from one mile east of Castroville to Route 101 near Prunedale as officially designated on September 14, 1972.
Between Castroville and Prunedale the route narrows to a heavily traveled two-lane road.
Castroville is known for its artichoke crop and calls itself the Artichoke Center of the World.

byways.name: Route 160, Sacramento River Delta
byways.where: SR 160 from the Contra Costa County line along the Sacramento River to the south Sacramento city limit (PM L0.0 to 35.0), Sacramento County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 160 from the Contra Costa county line to the south Sacramento city limit as officially designated on October 3, 1969.
The highway runs on the Sacramento River levees, crossing on the 1923 Isleton Bridge and the 1923 Paintersville Bridge, both bascule bridges, and passing Walnut Grove.
In 1922 the Victory Highway Association chose this river route, promoted as the "Netherlands Route", for the Victory Highway west of Sacramento.

byways.name: Route 163, Cabrillo Freeway through Balboa Park
byways.where: SR 163 from the south to the north boundary of Balboa Park (PM 0.95 to 2.18), San Diego

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 163 through Balboa Park as officially designated on April 24, 1992.

The Balboa Park section opened in 1948 and was the first freeway in San Diego County; it is built to parkway standards with a wide grassy median with trees and sharp curves, passing under the Cabrillo Bridge.

byways.name: Route 168, Bishop Creek
byways.where: SR 168 from Camp Sabrina (Lake Sabrina) down Bishop Creek to Brockman Lane on the Paiute-Shoshone reservation at Bishop (PM R0.0 to 16.3), Inyo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 168 from Camp Sabrina to Brockman Lane on the Paiute-Shoshone Indian Reservation near Bishop as officially designated on June 19, 1970.

The eastern segment of SR 168 begins at Lake Sabrina on the eastern slope of the Sierra Nevada and runs east to Bishop; the stretch from Lake Sabrina to Aspendell is closed to most vehicles in winter.
Lake Sabrina was created in 1907-08 by damming the middle fork of Bishop Creek to supply hydroelectric plants.

byways.review: Not the Ancient Bristlecone Scenic Byway: the catalog road ancient-bristlecone-scenic-byway-route-168-2303 is drawn on SR 168 east of Big Pine (White Mountains), which is only "Eligible" in the Caltrans list. Wikipedia wrongly equates the two. Caltrans spells "Pauite-Shos"; the where field uses the standard spelling Paiute-Shoshone.

byways.name: Route 180, Kings Canyon
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Forest Scenic Byway, Kings Canyon)
byways.where: SR 180 from the Alta Main Canal near Minkler to General Grant Grove, and from Grant Grove to the Kings Canyon National Park boundary near Cedar Grove (PM 78.6 to 137.9), Fresno and Tulare counties

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 180 from the Alta Main Canal near Minkler to the Kings Canyon National Park boundary near Cedar Grove, in two parts around General Grant Grove, as officially designated on October 15, 2015.
The route begins at the Hume Lake Ranger Station at 2,000 feet, climbs to 6,500 feet at Kings Canyon National Park, then descends 2,700 feet to the Kings River; the road ends just past Cedar Grove.
The stretch below the Hume Lake turnoff to Roads End closes in winter, typically November to April.

byways.review: The state designation (2015) starts farther west, near Minkler, than the USFS byway the catalog line follows (from Hume Lake Ranger Station area). Caltrans dates it October 15, 2015; Wikipedia says 2016.

byways.name: Route 190, Death Valley
byways.designation: State Scenic Highway (also National Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SR 190 across Death Valley National Park from the west to the east boundary (PM 42.4 to 124.4), Inyo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 190 across Death Valley as officially designated on May 10, 1968, with an extension to the west park boundary added January 7, 2002.

The highway drops into the Panamint Valley, crosses Towne Pass to Stovepipe Wells, passes Furnace Creek near the Badwater turnoff, and leaves the valley up Furnace Creek Wash, where flash floods close it at least once a year.
In late 1849 and early 1850 the Death Valley '49ers followed roughly the route of present SR 190 into Death Valley from Death Valley Junction.

byways.name: Route 247, High Desert (Barstow to Yucca Valley)
byways.where: SR 247 (Old Woman Springs Road and Barstow Road) between Yucca Valley and Barstow, four segments between PM 4.0 and 76.0, San Bernardino County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Route 247, Barstow to Yucca Valley, as officially designated (designation no. 62) in four segments between postmiles 4 and 76.
Caltrans designated State Route 247 from Barstow to Yucca Valley as a scenic byway in October 2025; the corridor passes the Ord Mountains, Lucerne Dry Lake, Black Lava Butte and Joshua trees.
Old Woman Springs takes its name from an 1856 survey party's encounter with elderly Native American women camped near present-day Lucerne Valley.

byways.review: Newest designation (October 2025). The Caltrans XLSX lists four segments without a date; the GIS layer has a single Officially Designated feature (Scenic_Miles 0, line about 58 mi long). Wikipedia still says it is not designated.

byways.name: Route 280, Junipero Serra Freeway
byways.where: I-280 from the Santa Clara County line to the north city limit of San Bruno (PM R0.0 to R21.8), San Mateo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists I-280 from the Santa Clara county line to the north city limit of San Bruno as officially designated on April 28, 1980.

The Junipero Serra Freeway has been called the "World's Most Beautiful Freeway" since its dedication; it runs just inside the rim of the San Andreas Fault rift valley and overlooks Crystal Springs Reservoir.
A 26-foot faux-sandstone statue of Junípero Serra was placed at the Crystal Springs Rest Area in 1975.

byways.name: Route 395, Inyo County
byways.where: US 395 from Fort Independence to Fish Springs Road (PM 77.3 to 96.6), Inyo County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists US 395 from Fort Independence to Fish Springs Road as officially designated on July 30, 1970.
North of Independence the highway passes the Fort Independence Indian Reservation and Tinemaha Reservoir, near where the Los Angeles Aqueduct takes water from the Owens River.

byways.name: Route 395, Mono County
byways.where: US 395 from the Inyo County line to south of Walker, in five segments (PM R0.0 to 104.8), Mono County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists US 395 from the Inyo county line to south of Walker, in five segments, as officially designated on November 9, 1971.
In Mono County the highway passes Crowley Lake, crosses the Long Valley Caldera and Deadman Summit (8,036 feet), runs beside Mono Lake at Lee Vining, and crosses Conway Summit near the Bodie turnoff.
North of Bridgeport it crosses 7,519-foot Devil's Gate Pass and descends the West Walker River toward Walker.

byways.review: The catalog line covers only about 12 miles near Mammoth; the designation runs about 100 miles. Replace with the Caltrans line.

byways.name: Route 580, MacArthur Freeway (Oakland)
byways.where: I-580 from the San Leandro city limit to Route 24 in Oakland (PM R34.5 to 45.2), Alameda County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists I-580 from the San Leandro city limit to Route 24 in Oakland as officially designated on June 25, 1976.
The MacArthur Freeway was built from 1960 and completed in May 1966; trucks over 4.5 tons are barred from it through Oakland.

byways.name: Route 680, Alameda County
byways.where: I-680 from Mission Boulevard in Fremont to the Contra Costa County line (PM R6.4 to R21.9), Alameda County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists I-680 from Mission Boulevard in Fremont to Bernal Avenue (June 15, 1978) and from Bernal Avenue to the Contra Costa county line (October 22, 1982) as officially designated.
I-680 crosses Mission Pass, the Sunol Grade, into the Sunol Valley; after September 2001 a US flag was painted on concrete on a hillside along the grade.

byways.name: Route 680, Contra Costa County
byways.where: I-680 from the Alameda County line to Route 24 in Walnut Creek (PM R0.0 to 14.4), Contra Costa County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists I-680 from the Alameda county line to Route 24 in Walnut Creek as officially designated on October 22, 1982.
I-680 heads north through the San Ramon Valley along the Calaveras Fault, through San Ramon, Danville and Alamo to Walnut Creek.

byways.name: Laureles Grade Road
byways.where: From SR 68 to Carmel Valley Road, Monterey County

facts.fact: Caltrans lists Laureles Grade Road as an officially designated County Scenic Highway (1969).

byways.review: County road, not drawn in the state network; the Caltrans GIS layer carries it with Official_Status "County Route". Blurb not written yet.

byways.name: Arroyo Seco Historic Parkway (Route 110)
byways.where: SR 110 from downtown Los Angeles to Pasadena

facts.fact: Mostly opened in 1940 alongside the Arroyo Seco between Los Angeles and Pasadena, it is one of the oldest freeways in the United States and was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 2011.

byways.review: The catalog and Wikipedia call it a State Scenic Highway, but it is not in the Caltrans officially designated list; the GIS layer marks it "Federal Byway".

byways.name: Tioga Road / Big Oak Flat Road
byways.where: SR 120 through Yosemite National Park over Tioga Pass to Lee Vining

facts.fact: Tioga Pass, at 9,945 feet, is the highest highway pass in California; in heavy snow years the road has stayed closed into late July.
Tuolumne Meadows lies less than seven miles southwest of the pass, inside Yosemite National Park.

byways.review: Catalog lists it as a California State Scenic Highway, but Route 120 is only "Eligible" in the Caltrans list (GIS marks it "Federal Byway").

byways.name: Volcanic Legacy Scenic Byway
byways.where: About 500 miles from Lassen Volcanic National Park north past Mount Shasta and Medicine Lake into Oregon

facts.fact: A 500-mile All-American Road from California to Oregon taking in Lassen Volcanic National Park, Mount Shasta, Medicine Lake, Lava Beds National Monument and Crater Lake.

byways.name: Ancient Bristlecone Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 168 east of Big Pine and White Mountain Road, Inyo National Forest

facts.fact: The White Mountains are arid desert yet hold the bristlecone pines.

Living bristlecones in the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest exceed 4,000 years of age, with views of the Great Basin; the visitor center is at Schulman Grove, and the nearest food, water or fuel is in Big Pine.

byways.review: Catalog designations list this as a California State Scenic Highway, but this stretch of SR 168 is only Eligible; the officially designated SR 168 segment is Bishop Creek, listed in the state program with bywayId null.

byways.name: Bigfoot Scenic Byway

facts.fact: The Bigfoot Scenic Byway runs along the Klamath River on Highway 96 from Happy Camp to Orleans.

byways.review: The catalog line runs farther (82 mi, bbox reaches 41.8N), so it may follow the longer Bigfoot route described by other sources.

facts.fact: Incorporates parts of Highway 89 out of McCloud and Highway 49 northeast to Medicine Lake; snow shuts the route around November to all vehicles except snowmobiles and snow cats.

byways.name: Rim of the World Scenic Byway

facts.fact: This 110-mile route traverses the rim of the San Bernardino Mountains from Cajon Pass to San Gorgonio Pass and uses portions of Highways 138, 18 and 38; it is open year-round but chains may be needed in winter.

byways.review: The Route 38 State Scenic Highway (Onyx Summit stretch) is part of this byway; it is listed in the state program with bywayId null.

facts.fact: The Sierra Heritage Scenic Byway follows Highway 168 from Clovis up the western slope of the Sierra Nevada to Kaiser Pass Meadow at about 9,000 feet; it is 70 miles long.
The Sierra Vista Scenic Byway starts near North Fork and runs 100 miles through the forest, ending near Oakhurst; it takes about 5 hours to drive.

byways.name: State of Jefferson Scenic Byway

facts.fact: The State of Jefferson Scenic Byway follows Highway 96 from Pioneer Bridge to Happy Camp and then Greyback Road to O'Brien, Oregon, at US 199.

byways.review: Catalog line is only 16.5 mi near the Oregon line (Greyback Road section).

facts.fact: The Pine Valley Overlook was a borrow pit during construction of the Sunrise Highway in 1937.
Desert View Picnic Area looks down on the desert 6,000 feet below; the El Prado cabin, a one-room log cabin built in 1912, was long the only national forest station in the Cleveland.
Begins in the historic mining town of Weaverville and ends on Interstate 5 just north of Weed; a self-guided auto tour brochure leads drivers through 17 stops.
Follows Highway 299 west from Shasta near Redding to Blue Lake near Arcata; designated the Trinity Scenic Byway in October 1991 with the theme "From the Valley Oaks to the Redwood Coast".

byways.name: Saline Valley Road
byways.review: Saline Valley now lies inside Death Valley National Park (NPS), so the BLM label may be historical; check.

issues: Grouping is mine: Caltrans designates 74 route segments (XLSX rows), not named roads. I merged contiguous segments of one route in one area (e.g. Route 1 Big Sur plus Carmel River to Route 68; I-5 and I-580 West Side Freeway; Routes 74 and 243 as Palms to Pines) into 48 members. Names are descriptive, not official, except where Caltrans uses one (Topanga Canyon, Gaviota Coast).

Ancient Bristlecone (catalog ancient-bristlecone-scenic-byway-route-168-2303) is labelled California State Scenic Highway in the catalog and Wikipedia, but the officially designated SR 168 segment is Camp Sabrina to Bishop (Bishop Creek), west of Bishop. The catalog line is east of Big Pine in the White Mountains, which Caltrans lists only as Eligible. Remove the state designation from the catalog road; draw Bishop Creek from the Caltrans layer.

Arroyo Seco Historic Parkway (110) and Tioga Road/Big Oak Flat Road (120) are labelled California State Scenic Highway in the catalog but are not in the Caltrans officially designated list (110 absent; 120 Eligible). The GIS layer carries both as Federal Byway features. Listed under the national program.
Route 395 Mono County: catalog line (route-395-mono-county-10688) is 12 mi around Mammoth; the designation is about 100 mi from the Inyo line to south of Walker. Replace with the Caltrans line.
Route 91: catalog line is 37.6 mi into Riverside County; only about 4 to 5 mi (Route 55 to east Anaheim city limit) is designated. Replace with the Caltrans line.
Route 24: catalog name says Alameda County, but the designated stretch is Contra Costa County (Caldecott east portal to I-680). Line is in the right place.

Route 12 (21 mi vs 11.6 designated) and Route 140 (44 mi vs 27 designated) catalog lines run beyond the designated segments; Kings Canyon catalog line follows the USFS byway, while the 2015 state designation starts farther west near Minkler.
Route 247 was designated in October 2025 (Scenic America news item; Caltrans XLSX lists it with no date, designation no. 62). No Caltrans announcement page found. Wikipedia still says not designated.

Route 38 (Onyx Summit stretch) is part of the USFS Rim of the World Scenic Byway and Route 49 in Sierra County is part of the USFS Yuba-Donner Scenic Byway (not in catalog); both left with bywayId null and gisValue so the state stretch can be drawn from the Caltrans layer.

Catalog road pacific-coast-highway-california-s-route-1-12744 (799 mi, "California State Scenic Byway") is not a designation; only five stretches of Route 1 are officially designated. Left out of all programs; consider demoting it to a classic drive.

Catalog road ramona-expressway-2181 ("State Scenic Backway") is not in the Caltrans list (official or county); its source listing (scenicbyways.info 2181) calls it only "Other Scenic Road". Left out of all programs; probably should be dropped or reclassed.

Catalog road wild-horse-canyon-scenic-backcountry-byway-2175 has the wrong designation ("State Scenic Backway"); it is an NPS backcountry road in Mojave National Preserve. Listed under an NPS program with the preserve home page as url.

BLM pages (blm.gov/visit/chimney-peak-back-country-byway, buckhorn-back-country-byway, barrel-springs-back-country-byway) return 403 to both curl and WebFetch, so they could not be checked and urls are null. Bradshaw Trail, Parker Dam Road and Saline Valley pages were not found at guessed slugs. No BLM blurbs written.

USFS byways with no url or blurb yet: Emigrant Trail, Feather River, Lassen, Lee Vining Canyon, Smith River. The new fs.usda.gov/r05 site has no page at the obvious slugs; Angeles Crest and Carson Pass state members also lack a USFS page.

County Scenic Highways (7, from the Caltrans 2015 PDF) are included as a second program with gisValue from the Caltrans layer but no blurbs yet. Drop the program if the chapter should list only state routes.

Most state members have url null: Caltrans has no per-highway pages, only the program page, the XLSX and the GIS experience app. Big Sur url is the Big Sur Chamber of Commerce (tourism), Ebbetts Pass is the byway association, Route 52 is Mission Trails Regional Park.
